target_customer: Independent convenience store owners in the US
problem: Independent c-store owners lack real-time visibility into transactions, pricing and scan data across their stores and cannot easily manage fuel prices, loyalty and brand data exchange.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for store owners (Basic and Standard plans) plus a hardware module and brand data exchange
product_category: Convenience store back-office software and analytics

founders.name: Mit Patel
education: Auburn University, mechanical engineering and accounting (senior in 2021)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he has a backend and network engineering background and grew up managing his family's convenience stores.

founders.name: Daniel Mazur
founders.background_notes: YC page says he has an analytics and design background and oversees operations. Both founders are 2017 Hoover High School graduates per Auburn.

competitors.name: Skupos
competitors.what: Analytics platform for convenience stores, distributors and brands
competitors.traction_then: Reported to have more than doubled customers in months before June 2019
competitors.funding_then: 26.8M Series B in June 2019, about 37M total

technical_complexity.rationale: Real-time connection to multiple point of sale systems and fuel brand data formats with analytics is standard engineering with integration difficulty, built by student founders.

defensibility.rationale: POS integrations, scan data relationships with brands and store-owner trust create some lock-in, but Skupos and POS vendors offered overlapping analytics.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Site lists Verifone and Gilbarco as partners, not rivals; no source shows anyone copying or buying SwiftSku.

market_need_then: Independent c-stores lacked remote monitoring and brand scan data programs; the founder grew up in his family's convenience stores and the company reported 250+ customers by June 2021.

branding.domain_note: Uses swiftsku.com, exact name .com; history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly, practical and benefit-focused, with the line Your Data is YOUR Data and support in English, Hindi and Gujarati

branding.brand_signature: Support for store owners in Hindi and Gujarati
branding.community_and_virality: Won the Rice Business Plan Competition grand prize in 2021, covered by Rice and Auburn news.

brand_strength.rationale: Known to c-store owners and in startup competition coverage, but no evidence of wider brand recognition.

outcome_analysis: SwiftSku was conceived in August 2019 by two Auburn students, one raised in his family's convenience stores. It won the 2021 Rice Business Plan Competition with a 350,000 dollar investment, joined YC Winter 2021 and reports 35 staff and thousands of customers on its site. It is Active with no exit and no priced venture round found, so funding is only partly known. Skupos was a better funded rival in the same niche.
notes: Auburn says a 3.2 million dollar total came from competition winnings plus a YC investment, not itemized; Seedtable shows 3.0M and CB Insights shows 530K across three rounds, conflicting and aggregator only so not recorded. The Rice prize was recorded as a grant dated April 2021 because the competition ran April 6 to 9 and prizes included other cash awards (50K, 25K, 10K) not recorded as rounds. The YC investment amount is not stated. CB Insights lists Birmingham Alabama while YC lists New York. Dorm Room Fund and Eppes Creek Ventures appear only in CB Insights snippets.
